tasks.short: Tell riders how to fasten belts and bars, fasten them for those who need help, and check every restraint before the ride starts.

steps.what: Attendant gives patrons directions for fastening belts and lap bars
Attendant fastens safety devices for small children and riders who need help
Attendant checks by hand that every restraint is locked before dispatch

tasks.design: No change is proposed: fastening and checking restraints is hands-on safety work at every cycle. Where rides have restraint sensors they already back up the hand check, and the hand check stays.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocks it; this is physical safety work.
tasks.enabler_now: Not applicable; there is no paperwork in this task.
tasks.still_hard: Everything: each rider and each restraint needs a person's eyes and hands.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing the child who slipped under the bar.

reach.learn: Whether check routines can be shared across rides.

evidence.claim: Ride restraint sensors back up but do not replace the hand check by staff.
Fastening restraints touches no high-risk AI area; no AI is used.

assumptions: Boundary: from riders seated to restraints checked; ride operation is outside.
Input contract: none; the ride's check routine comes from the safety coordinator on paper.
No monitoring of staff is added.
All steps stay as they are.
unknowns: Share of the shift spent at the loading platform.

incremental.description: No new work: the design adds no tool or record to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The task is entirely hands-on safety work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Call out to passers-by, explain games and prizes, and make announcements about shows and games over the speakers.

steps.what: Attendant announces attractions to passers-by to entice customers to games
Attendant describes the game and the prizes
Attendant reads show and game announcements over the speakers from notes

tasks.design: Routine announcements are recorded once and played over the speakers at set times from the day's show schedule ({OTHER}), so the attendant only announces specials live. Calling out and explaining games stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every announcement was read live from notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Speaker systems can play recorded messages on a schedule.
tasks.still_hard: Enticing visitors is a live performance; recorded messages are easy to ignore.
tasks.human_edge: The banter that gets a hesitant teenager to try one throw.

reach.learn: Whether scheduled messages fill shows as well as live calls.

evidence.claim: Public address systems can play recorded messages on a schedule.
Recorded announcements touch no high-risk AI area.

assumptions: Boundary: from passers-by to announcements made; running the game is outside.
Input contract: show schedule kept by the facility manager; recordings made once by staff; fallback is reading live.
Live calling and explaining do not change.
unknowns: How many announcements a day are routine.
research_questions: Do scheduled messages change show attendance?

incremental.description: Attendant records new announcements when shows change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is live calling and talking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take court and lane bookings, write them in the planner, sort out clashes, block league slots, tell players about cancellations and take fees.

steps.what: Players phone or come to the desk to book a court or lane
Attendant takes booking requests for courts and lanes by phone and at the desk
Attendant writes bookings in the paper planner
Attendant sorts out double bookings and swaps
Attendant schedules the use of recreation facilities for leagues and club blocks each season
Attendant phones booked players about weather cancellations
Attendant collects court and lane fees at the desk

tasks.design: Players book and pay courts and lanes online in a facility booking system ({OTHER}) that shows live availability and cannot double-book; desk and phone bookings go into the same system. League blocks repeat for the season, and a weather cancellation sends one message to everyone booked; swaps and special requests stay with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bookings lived in a paper planner fed by phone calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking systems with online payment and live availability are standard for sports facilities; attraction ticketing runs web shop and till on one back end.
tasks.still_hard: Regulars who phone need help; leagues bring special requests.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a slot for a club that just lost its court.
tasks.altitude: The attendant handles exceptions instead of every booking.

reach.learn: Whether booking data show which slots to price differently.

evidence.claim: Facility booking systems take online bookings with live availability and payment.
An attraction ticketing system runs web shop, gate till and kiosks on one back end with live reporting.
Booking records hold names and contact details; keep them only as long as needed.

assumptions: Boundary: from booking request to fees collected; pricing is outside.
Input contract: courts, lanes, prices and opening times set by the facility manager; league requests from the clubs; fallback is the paper planner.
Player time is outside the attendant's savings.
Swaps and special requests stay with the attendant.
unknowns: Share of bookings that would move online.
research_questions: Do no-shows fall with online payment?

already_counted.description: Attendant checks season blocks before publishing.

incremental.description: Players book and pay courts and lanes online themselves (work moved from the attendant's bookings).

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Facilities with many phone-only regulars keep more desk work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take orders and serve refreshments, take payment, restock the kiosk and count stock and cash at closing.

steps.what: Attendant takes orders and serves refreshments to customers
Attendant takes cash and card payment at the kiosk till
Attendant restocks the kiosk from the store
Attendant counts stock and cash on a sheet at closing

tasks.design: The kiosk till ({OTHER}) is linked to the card reader and to the facility's ticketing back end, so sales and expected stock are known; at closing the attendant counts only the cash and spot-checks stock against the till's list. Serving and restocking stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales were rung up on a stand-alone till and stock counted on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Attraction ticketing systems link tills to one back end with live reporting.
tasks.still_hard: Cash customers keep the count; stock lists are only right if every sale is rung up.
tasks.human_edge: A friendly word with an ice cream on a hot day.

reach.learn: Whether till data cut waste of perishable snacks.

evidence.claim: An attraction ticketing system links web shop, tills and kiosks on one back end with live reporting.
Till records touch no high-risk AI area.

assumptions: Boundary: from order to closing count; buying stock is outside.
Input contract: item list and prices set by the facility manager in the till; fallback is the paper sheet.
Serving and restocking do not change.
Counts are per kiosk, not per attendant.
unknowns: Share of cash payments at the kiosk.
research_questions: Do stock differences shrink with till-based lists?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is serving customers in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The recreation attendant keeps safety, serving and showmanship; bookings, announcements and counts take less time.
role.ambitious_version: An attendant who is out with visitors, not tied to a planner or a till.
